name: Hagar, and the God who seeth
charge: Returning and submitting when the angel sent her back; and calling him Thou God seest me
summary: An Egyptian bondwoman given to Abram by her mistress, despised her when she conceived and was dealt with hardly until she fled. The angel of the Lord found her by a fountain in the wilderness, called her by name and by her station, told her to return and submit, and gave her a promise for her son. She named the Lord that spake unto her and called the well Beer-lahai-roi. Sent away years later with bread and a bottle of water, she was met again when the water was spent.
offense: She was told to go back to a house she had run from and to a mistress who had dealt hardly with her (Genesis 16:6), and she went. The angel gave her both a command to return and a promise that her seed would be multiplied beyond numbering (Genesis 16:9-10). Her son would be called Ishmael because the Lord had heard her affliction; his life and relations with his brethren were foretold before his birth (Genesis 16:11-12). The record does not conceal her fault either, that when she saw she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes, so the case is of a woman corrected and restored rather than of one wronged only.
judgment: The angel found her by a fountain in the wilderness and addressed the servant whom the household dispute had driven away (Genesis 16:7-8). She answered the encounter with the name, Thou God seest me (Genesis 16:13). The well was called after it (Genesis 16:14) and was still known by that name when the account was written. When the bread and the water were gone and she had set the child down and lifted up her voice and wept, God heard the voice of the lad, renewed the promise that he would become a great nation, and opened her eyes to a well of water (Genesis 21:17-19). She filled the bottle and gave him drink, and God was with him as he grew (Genesis 21:20-21). The covenant inheritance was appointed through Isaac, but Ishmael was not forgotten: God had also promised Abraham a nation from this son (Genesis 21:12-13).
